name: Edit
description: A condition of a webpage when it is being modified or edited by a user. This state is often indicated by a change in the webpage's appearance, such as a highlighted menu item or tab.

name: Filter & Sorting
description: A feature on a website or application that allows users to narrow down or organize content based on certain criteria. This design pattern is often represented by a drop-down menu or set of checkboxes and may include options for sorting content by date, relevance, or other factors.

name: Success
description: A condition of a webpage when an action or process has been completed successfully.

name: Loading & Connecting
description: A condition of a webpage when it is in the process of loading or connecting to a server or other resource. This state is often indicated by a change in the webpage's appearance, such as a loading spinner or message.

name: Permission
description: A condition of a webpage when a user is being asked to provide permission or consent for an action or process.

name: Confirmation
description: A condition of a webpage when a user is being asked to confirm an action or provide further information.

name: Empty State
description:
A user interface element that is displayed when a list or collection of items is empty or has no data to display. It is typically presented as a placeholder or default view that is displayed when no other content is available.

Other names: blank state, zero data state

name: Error
description: A page state in which an error or problem has occurred on a webpage. This state is often indicated through visual changes, such as an error message or notification. This error could be caused by a variety of issues, including server errors, user input errors, or other technical issues.

name: Feedback & Survey
description: A feature that allows users to provide feedback or answer questions about a product, service, or experience on a website or application. This pattern may include a survey form or rating system and may be used to gather user insights or improve the user experience.

name: Dark Mode
description:
A design feature that allows users to switch the color scheme of a website or application to a darker hue, typically for the purposes of reducing eye strain or conserving battery life on mobile devices.

Note: The dark mode tag is used to identify websites that offer both a light and dark mode option. It is not applicable to websites that only have a dark appearance.

name: FAQ
description: A webpage or section that provides answers to common questions about a product, service, or company. This page is often organized by topic and includes a list of questions with corresponding answers.

name: Payment Method
description: A feature that allows users to select and input their preferred method of payment on a website or application. This pattern may include options for credit card, debit card, or other payment methods and may also include options for inputting billing and shipping information.

name: Booking
description:
A feature that allows users to reserve or schedule services or appointments through a website or application. This pattern typically includes options for selecting dates, times, and payment methods.

Other names: reservation, scheduling, appointment booking.

name: Shopping
description: The Shopping design pattern usually appears as a grid or list of product cards, each showing a clear product image, product name, price, and often a short description or key features. Each product card typically includes interactive elements such as an “Add to Cart” or “Buy Now” button, and sometimes icons for favorite, compare, or quick view. Prices may show discounts with original and sale prices side by side. The layout is clean and organized, allowing users to browse multiple products at once. Product cards may also display ratings with stars, availability status, or tags like “New” or “Sale.” At the top or side of the page, there are often filtering and sorting controls to help users narrow down choices by categories, price range, brand, or other attributes. You can identify the Shopping pattern by its consistent display of multiple product items with images, prices, and clear purchase actions arranged in a browsable format.

name: Email Subscription
description: A service that enables a user to receive regular emails from a website or organization. The emails may include news, updates, promotions, or other information relevant to the user.

name: Like & Reactions
description: A design patterns that allow users to express their approval or support of a piece of content or idea on a website or application. These patterns may include a like button or upvote button that users can click to show their support.

name: Chat & Messages
description: A feature that allows users to communicate with each other or with customer service representatives through a messaging interface on a website or application. This pattern may include options for text, audio, or video messaging and may also include features for organizing and storing messages.

name: Reviews & Rating
description:
The Reviews & Rating design pattern typically appears as a vertical or horizontal list of user-generated feedback entries, each including a user name or avatar, a star rating (usually 1 to 5 stars), and a written review or comment. Visually, the star rating is often displayed prominently near the top or next to the user’s name to quickly convey the overall score. Each review card may also include the date of the review, and sometimes additional details like pros and cons, photos, or user location. The layout is clean and structured to allow easy scanning of multiple reviews. At the top or side, there’s often an average rating summary with an aggregated star score and total number of reviews.

This pattern differs from Testimonials, which are usually more curated, longer, and more formal statements from selected users or clients, often highlighted separately with more emphasis on the person or company giving the testimonial. Reviews are typically more numerous, less formal, and come from a wider variety of users, reflecting real and diverse opinions. You can avoid confusing them by remembering that Reviews & Rating sections focus on many short, star-scored opinions displayed together, while Testimonials are fewer, more polished, and treated like endorsements often presented as quotes or featured blocks.

name: Achievements & Awards
description: A page on a website or application that displays a user's accomplishments or recognition on the site. This page may include badges, trophies, or other symbols of achievement and may also include details about how the achievements were earned.

name: Comments
description: Comments are a design pattern that allows users to leave their thoughts, opinions, or feedback on a piece of content or idea on a website or application. This pattern may include a comment section or form where users can enter their comments and may also include features for responding to or moderating comments.

name: Add & Invite People
description:
A design pattern that enables users to add or invite others to join a group or project on a website or application. This pattern is often represented by a button or icon and may include options for selecting specific users or sending invitations through email or other channels.

Other names: add member, invite member, join group.

name: Files
description: Managing, uploading, downloading, or sharing files on a website or application through features for organizing, previewing, and editing files. This pattern may also include options for collaborating with other users.

name: Testimonials
description:
The Testimonials design pattern typically appears as a section featuring one or several highlighted quotes or statements from customers or users, often styled to stand out on the page. Visually, testimonials are usually presented inside distinct cards, blocks, or bubbles with quotation marks to emphasize the quoted text. Each testimonial includes the person’s name, sometimes their photo or avatar, and their title or company affiliation to add credibility. The text is often longer and more detailed than in reviews, written in a more polished, narrative style. Testimonials are usually arranged in a carousel, grid, or vertical list with ample spacing to draw attention to each individual story.

This pattern differs from Reviews & Rating, which typically shows many short, user-generated comments accompanied by star ratings. Reviews are more numerous, informal, and focus on scores and brief opinions. Reviews are NOT testimonials. 

Testimonials can NOT contain only logos without text!

name: Event
description: A type of web page that presents information about a planned event, including details such as the date, time, location, and purpose of the event. It may also provide ticketing and registration options, as well as information about the event's organizers.

name: Article & Text
description: A web page that primarily consists of written content, such as a news article, blog post, or research report. It may include headlines, subheadings, and body text, as well as images and other multimedia elements.

name: Audio Player
description: A interface that allows users to play audio files. It typically includes controls like play/pause, skip, and volume, as well as a display showing the current track and progress.

name: Stats
description: Refer to the presentation of numerical data or statistics in a clear and visually appealing way. This can be achieved through the use of various design elements such as graphs, charts, and infographics, which allow for easy interpretation and understanding of the data being presented.

name: Video Player
description: The Video Player pattern enables users to watch video content within an interface. It typically includes controls such as Play/Pause, volume, timeline scrubber, full-screen toggle, and playback speed adjustment. May also feature subtitles, resolution settings, and chapter markers. The play button is commonly centered and styled prominently, often as a white or black triangle on a circular background. Used across media platforms, tutorials, product demos, and ads.

name: Calling
description:
A Calling pattern (such as video call, audio call, or phone call) is a user interface layout designed to present live information about an active conversation. It shows details like the participant’s identity, call duration, and controls to mute, hold, or end the call. This pattern creates a focused space for managing communication during the ongoing interaction, commonly found in messaging apps, conferencing software, or phone systems.

DO NOT identify Call as CTA or Call To Action!

name: Camera & Scanner
description: A camera design pattern is a design element that allows users to take photos within an app or website. It may include features such as a viewfinder, flash, or focus controls. A scanner design pattern is a similar element that allows users to scan items such as QR codes or documents.

name: Date & Time
description: A feature that allows users to select or input dates and times within an app or website. It may take the form of a calendar view, a dropdown menu, or a text field and may include features such as timezone selection or date formatting options.

name: Location & Address
description: A pattern that allows users to input or select a physical location within an app or website. It may be presented as a map view, a search field, or a dropdown menu and may include features such as geolocation or address validation.

name: Calendar
description: A tool for users to manage and organize their schedules and tasks. It may take the form of a grid view, a list view, or a timeline view, and may include features such as date navigation, event creation, and reminder notifications.

name: Text Editing
description: A process of making changes to written text, including correcting errors, formatting the text, and adding or removing content. This process can be done manually or with software or tools.

name: Timer & Clock
description: A tool for users to display and track the current time. It may take the form of a digital display, a dial, or an analog face, and may include features such as date display, alarms, and timezone selection.

name: Timeline & History
description: A graphical representation of a sequence of events, displaying them in chronological order and often illustrating the relationships between events. It can be presented in a variety of formats, such as a linear graph, list view, or calendar view.

name: Ads & Promo Offer
description: A marketing materials or promotions designed to advertise a product, service, or event. They may be displayed on websites, social media, email, or other channels, and may include discounts, coupons, or other incentives to encourage the user to take action.

name: Promo Code
description:
A design pattern that allows users to enter a special code to receive a discount or other promotion on a website or application. This code is typically entered at checkout or during the purchase process.

Other names: coupon code, discount code, voucher code.

name: Upload & Download
description: The Upload & Download design pattern often appears as a clearly defined rectangular or rounded area called a drop zone where users can drag and drop files to upload. This area is usually visually distinct with dashed or solid borders and may include an icon such as a cloud with an arrow pointing up (for upload) or down (for download). Inside or near the drop zone, there is typically instructional text like “Drag files here,” “Click to upload,” or “Drop files to start.” The interface often includes buttons for manually selecting files from the device, usually labeled “Browse” or “Select Files.” When files are uploaded, thumbnails, filenames, or progress bars appear within or below the drop zone, showing upload status or allowing users to cancel or remove files. For downloads, the pattern might show a clear button or link with a download icon and filename, sometimes accompanied by progress indicators. Visually, this pattern stands out with its interactive area dedicated to file transfer, clear icons representing upload or download, and dynamic feedback elements showing the status of the action.

name: Wish List & Bookmark
description:
A design pattern that enables users to save items or content for future reference or purchase. This pattern is commonly represented by a heart icon or a "wish list" button. A bookmark is a similar design pattern that allows users to save webpages or content for later reference, often represented by a bookmark icon or a "bookmark" button.

Other names: favorite, save for later.

name: Design Editing
description: A process of making modifications and refinements to the visual elements of a design. This may include adjusting colors, typography, layout, or other aesthetic elements to enhance the design's appeal and effectiveness.

name: Media Editing
description: A process of altering and refining audio, video, or other media content. This may include cutting and splicing together different clips, adding special effects or transitions, and adjusting audio levels or other technical elements.

name: Ban & Block
description: A design pattern is a feature that allows website or application administrators to prevent certain users from accessing the platform. This feature is often used to enforce rules or policies and can be implemented through the use of IP addresses or account bans.

name: Flag & Report
description:
A feature that enables users to report inappropriate content or issues they have encountered on a website or application. This design pattern is used to help maintain the integrity and quality of the platform.

Other names: report function, flag function, report tool.

name: Groups & Community
description: The Groups & Community design pattern is an interface element that facilitates user interaction, collaboration, and communication within a shared space, often focused on common interests or goals. It is typically presented as a dedicated section within an app or website where users can join, create, or participate in groups or discussions. This pattern is identifiable by features such as group listings, which often include a name, description, member count, and an option to join or request access. Once inside a group, users usually find a feed or a discussion board for sharing updates, asking questions, or posting content, often accompanied by engagement options like comments, likes, or reactions. It may also include tools for managing group members, such as roles or permissions, as well as features for events, polls, or file sharing to foster collaboration. Groups often display key metrics like activity levels or member contributions to highlight engagement. This pattern is commonly used in social networks, professional platforms, and collaborative tools, providing a clear space for fostering community-driven interactions and shared goals. You can recognize it by its structured approach to organizing users around specific topics or purposes with tools to facilitate communication and participation.

name: Share
description: A feature that allows users to share content from a website or application with others through social media or other platforms. This pattern is often represented by a button or icon that initiates the sharing process.

name: Followers & Following
description: A feature found on social media platforms and other websites that allows users to follow other users or content and see updates in their feed. This pattern is often represented by a "follow" button or icon and may also include a list of users that a user is following or that are following them.

name: Searching
description: A process of using a search to locate specific information, content, or products on a website or application. This process may involve entering a search term or query and filtering the results based on certain criteria.

name: Checklist & To Do
description:
The Checklist & To-Do design pattern typically appears as a vertical list of tasks or items, each accompanied by a checkbox or toggle to mark completion. Visually, each item in the list includes a short label or description of the task, often followed by icons or buttons for actions like editing, deleting, or adding subtasks. When an item is marked as complete, it may show a visual change, such as a checkmark in the box, strikethrough text, or a faded/greyed-out appearance to indicate its completion.

The list is often preceded by a title or header like “To-Do List” or “Checklist” and may include controls for adding new tasks, such as an input field with a "+" button. Some variations may feature progress indicators, such as a percentage bar or a numerical counter showing how many tasks are complete out of the total. You can identify the Checklist & To-Do pattern by its structured format, interactive checkboxes, and the ability to track, manage, and visualize progress through task completion.

name: Food & Recipe
description: A page on a website that is dedicated to sharing information about food and cooking. This page may include recipes, cooking tips, and information about ingredients and nutrition.

name: Select
description:
A condition of a webpage when it is actively being chosen or selected by a user. This state is often indicated by a change in the webpage's appearance, such as a highlighted menu item or tab.

Other names: active state, selected state, chosen state.

name: Money Transfer
description: The Money Transfer pattern allows users to transfer money between accounts — either internally (e.g., between a user’s own accounts) or externally (e.g., to another person or bank). It typically involves data input, validation, confirmation, and success/error feedback. It includes inputs like the recipient’s name, account number, transfer amount, and source account. It also features buttons such as “Send” or “Transfer” and may include currency conversion.

name: Mini Game
description: A compact, interactive game that is incorporated into the website for the user's enjoyment. These games are usually designed to be simple and quick to play, and may be used for entertainment or to engage the user with the website.

name: Add & Create
description: A process of adding new content or creating new pages within a website or application. This may involve adding new text, images, or other elements to existing pages, or creating entirely new pages to be added to the website or application.

name: Delete
description: A state that allows users to delete or remove items from a list or collection. It is typically triggered by a user action such as clicking a delete button or selecting an item and activating a delete command.

name: Trash & Archive
description: A page that contains old or past content that is no longer actively displayed or updated. This content may include articles, blog posts, news items, or other types of information that has been superseded by more recent content.

name: Chat Bot
description: A program that is designed to simulate conversation with human users, often through messaging applications, websites, or mobile apps. Chat bots are often used to provide customer service or offer information to users in a conversational format.

name: Product Features
description: A webpage or section of a website that highlights the specific features or benefits of a product. This page may include details about the product's functionality, performance, or design and may also include images or videos demonstrating the features.

name: Templates
description: The Templates design pattern usually appears as a grid or list of rectangular cards or thumbnails, each representing a pre-made design, document, or layout that users can select and use. Visually, each template card shows a small preview image or screenshot that gives a quick idea of the style or content. Below or next to the preview, there is often a title or name of the template and sometimes a brief description or category label. The layout is clean and organized, allowing easy browsing and comparison between different options. Templates may be grouped by categories, tags, or filters, with navigation elements like tabs, dropdowns, or search bars nearby to help users find specific types of templates. You can identify this pattern by its repeated cards or thumbnails showing visual previews arranged neatly in rows or columns, designed to help users quickly pick a ready-made option to start from.

name: Trial & Freemium
description: Trial Subscription and Freemium models are ways to allow users to try a service before committing to a paid subscription. A Trial Subscription is a time-limited offer, where as Freemium is a feature limited offer. With Freemium, users can continue to use the service forever with a limited set of features, but with a Trial Subscription users can only use the service for a certain period of time and after that they need to subscribe to continue using the service.

name: Billing & Plans
description: The Billing & Plans pattern displays information about pricing tiers, subscription options, billing history, and payment settings. It often includes cards or tables showing plan names, features, prices, and billing frequency (monthly, yearly). Users can upgrade, downgrade, cancel, or change payment methods. May also show current plan status, invoices, trial periods, and renewal dates. Common in SaaS dashboards, account settings.

name: Press
description: The Press pattern presents official media coverage, announcements, and mentions of a company or product. It typically includes article headlines, publication names, dates, excerpts, and links to external sources. May be styled as cards, a list, or a grid layout. Often used on corporate or product sites in the press or media section to build trust and credibility. Can include press kits or downloadable assets.

name: Tutorial & Education
description: The Tutorial & Education pattern guides users through learning a concept, task, or product. It often includes step-by-step instructions, videos, tooltips, checklists, or interactive elements. Commonly used in onboarding, training modules, and help centers.

name: Size Guide
description: The Size Guide design pattern typically appears as a clear, organized chart or table that helps users understand sizing information, often for clothing, shoes, or products. Visually, it usually consists of labeled rows and columns with measurements like height, chest, waist, or shoe length, often accompanied by size labels such as S, M, L, XL, or numeric sizes like 6, 7, 8. The guide may include simple icons or illustrations showing how and where measurements are taken on the body or product, such as lines or arrows pointing to specific parts like chest, hips, or foot. Sometimes there are tabs or dropdowns to switch between different sizing systems (e.g., US, UK, EU) or categories like men’s, women’s, or kids’ sizes. The layout is clean and easy to scan, often presented as a grid with clear headings, making it easy for users to compare sizes and choose the right fit. You can identify a Size Guide by its structured table format, measurement labels, and helpful visual cues explaining sizing details.

name: Shortcuts
description: The Shortcuts pattern provides quick access to frequently used actions, pages, or tools. These can appear as buttons, icons, or tiles—often on the dashboard, homepage, or within a toolbar. Each shortcut typically includes a label and an icon, and is often styled to resemble keyboard keys (e.g., with rounded rectangular shapes, subtle shadows, or borders). May support customization (add/remove/edit) based on user preferences. Used to streamline navigation and reduce the number of steps to reach common tasks.

name: Suggestion & Similar Items
description: The Suggestion & Similar Items pattern displays recommended content, products, or entries based on user behavior, preferences, or related context. It typically includes thumbnails, titles, brief descriptions, and sometimes pricing or ratings. Often appears in carousels, side panels, or below primary content. Common in blogs, e-commerce, media platforms, and search interfaces.

name: Activity & Notification Feed
description: The Activity & Notification Feed design pattern appears as a vertical list or column of repeated cards or rows, each representing a separate event or notification. Visually, each item usually includes a small icon or user avatar on the left, a short text description summarizing the activity or notification, and a timestamp indicating when it happened. Different types of notifications may use distinct icons or colors to represent actions like likes, comments, new followers, or system alerts. Each entry often contains the user’s name, a brief message about the event, and sometimes a clickable link to related content. Some notifications also have action buttons such as “reply,” “mark as read,” or “delete” placed on the right side. The overall look is a clean, structured vertical feed with clear separation between items, icons, and timestamps, creating a continuous stream of updates that keep the user informed about recent activity or important alerts.

name: News Feed
description: The News Feed pattern displays a continuously updating list of content items, typically sorted by time, relevance, or personalization. It includes items like posts, articles, updates, or media. Each item may show a title, image, description, timestamp, and author or source. It often supports infinite scroll or pagination, as well as interactions like like, comment, share, or save. Commonly used in social networks, content platforms, and dashboards.

name: Augmented Reality
description: The Augmented Reality (AR) pattern integrates digital content into the physical world through the device’s camera view. It overlays 3D objects, labels, instructions, or effects onto real-time video from the user’s environment. Typically includes an AR viewer, interactive controls, placement guides, and sometimes a “View in Your Space” or “Start AR” button. Common in e-commerce (e.g., product try-ons or furniture previews), education, gaming, and navigation.

name: Task
description: The Task pattern represents a single actionable item or objective within a workflow, to-do list, or project. It typically includes a title or name, status indicator (e.g., checkbox, progress bar, tag), due date, and optional metadata like priority, assignee, or subtasks. Tasks may be grouped into lists or boards and support interactions like mark as complete, edit, reorder (often via drag & drop), or assign. Commonly used in productivity apps, dashboards, onboarding flows, and project management tools.

name: Browser
description: The Browser pattern provides a contained view for displaying web pages or web-based content within an app or platform. It often mimics a simplified web browser, including elements like an address bar, back/forward buttons, reload control, and loading indicators. May also show security indicators (like a lock icon) and permission prompts. Commonly used in mobile apps, embedded documentation, in-app browsing, or previewing links. Sometimes styled with a browser frame or header to visually separate it from native UI.

name: Audio & Video Recorder
description: The Audio & Video Recorder pattern allows users to capture audio or video directly within the interface using device hardware. It typically includes controls like “Record,” “Stop,” “Pause,” and “Play,” along with visual indicators for recording status (e.g., blinking dot, waveform, or timer). The primary record button is commonly styled in red to signal recording intent clearly. May also include device selection (microphone or camera), preview windows, and re-record options. Common in messaging apps, online forms, educational tools, and content creation platforms.

name: Drag & Drop
description: The Drag & Drop pattern allows users to click and hold an item, move it across the interface, and place it into a new location. It is used for rearranging, organizing, uploading files, or customizing layouts. Visual feedback includes highlighted drop zones, ghost elements, or cursor changes. A common drag handle icon is three horizontal lines (also known as a “grip” or “hamburger” drag icon), indicating that an element can be moved. Common in dashboards, file managers, builders, and multi-step workflows.

name: Draw
description:
The Draw design pattern is a user interface element that enables freehand drawing or annotation directly on a canvas or surface within an application. It is typically identifiable by the presence of a blank canvas or an image/document over which users can draw, along with a tool palette that provides drawing options.

The tool palette is often positioned at the top, bottom, or side of the canvas and includes recognizable icons for tools like a pen, pencil, brush, eraser, or shape tools (e.g., lines, rectangles, circles). The palette may also feature options for selecting colors, brush sizes, and opacity levels.

The canvas itself is interactive, allowing users to draw freeform strokes, often with visible smoothing or pressure sensitivity (if supported). Additional controls, such as undo/redo buttons, a clear/reset canvas button, or the ability to save/export drawings, are commonly included near the workspace.

You can identify the Draw pattern by its combination of a dedicated canvas for creating visual content and a floating or fixed toolbar with intuitive drawing controls, clearly tailored for freeform interaction.

name: Save
description: The Save pattern allows users to store their progress, preferences, or selected content for later access. It typically appears as a button or icon labeled “Save,” “Save Changes,” or represented by floppy disk icon. Used in forms, settings, documents, product pages, or user dashboards.

name: Pull to Action
description: The Pull to Action pattern enables users to trigger an action by pulling or swiping down on the top of a scrollable area—most commonly used for refreshing content (known as “pull to refresh”). It often includes visual cues like a downward arrow, loading spinner, or progress indicator that appears as the user pulls past a threshold. Common in mobile apps and touch interfaces, especially in feeds, inboxes, and lists. Can also trigger non-refresh actions in custom implementations.

name: Quickstart Guide
description: The Quickstart Guide pattern provides users with a short, focused set of steps to get started with a product, service, or workflow. It usually appears after signup or onboarding and highlights key actions through steps, cards, or a checklist. May include icons, brief descriptions, progress indicators. Often positioned on dashboards, welcome screens, or modals. Helps users reach early value quickly.

name: Kanban Board
description:
The Kanban Board design pattern has a distinctive visual layout with a series of vertical columns arranged side by side. Each column is typically labeled at the top to represent a specific stage of a workflow, such as "To Do," "In Progress," or "Done." Within each column, you’ll see rectangular cards stacked vertically. These cards are the tasks or items being tracked, and they usually include a title and sometimes additional details like a short description, tags, due dates, or assigned team members (often shown as small avatars).

The cards are interactive and can be dragged and dropped between columns to indicate their progression through the workflow. Many boards also use color-coded tags or labels on the cards for quick categorization. Columns might show counters at the top, indicating how many cards they contain, or include visual cues like progress bars or limits to the number of cards allowed.

Overall, a Kanban Board looks like a structured grid of labeled vertical sections with movable, stackable cards, making it easy to identify in any image or interface.

name: Swipe Actions
description: The Swipe Actions pattern allows users to perform quick contextual actions by swiping left or right on a list item, card, or row—most commonly on mobile. Typical actions include delete, archive, mark as read, pin, or snooze. Revealed actions may appear as icons with labels, color-coded for clarity (e.g., red for delete). Often used in email apps, task lists, messaging, and content management. Supports touch gestures and sometimes mouse events on desktop.

name: Leaderboard
description: The Leaderboard pattern displays a ranked list of users or entities based on performance, scores, or achievements. It typically includes data points like rank, name or avatar, score/value, and position changes. It may include visual highlights for top positions. Often used in games, contests, learning platforms, or community apps.

name: AI Assistant
description: The AI Assistant design pattern is an interface or feature that helps users complete tasks, answer questions, or provide recommendations using artificial intelligence. It is often identified by the presence of a conversational interface, a floating action button, or a dedicated section visually and functionally distinct from other parts of the UI. Typically, it includes a trigger or entry point, such as an icon like a chat bubble, robot, or magic wand, or a button labeled “Ask AI” or “Assistant,” often accessible across the app as a persistent floating button or within a menu. The assistant usually operates through a conversational interface where users can type questions or commands and receive responses in text, voice, or visual elements. It often adapts to the current screen or task, offering context-aware suggestions or answers. Many assistants provide pre-filled prompts or suggestions to guide users in interacting with the feature. Responses can include plain text, cards, or actionable items like quick buttons or links to other app sections. Some assistants support multimodal interaction, such as voice input or image recognition, and integrate with other app features to streamline workflows. This pattern is used to enhance productivity, simplify complex tasks, or provide a personalized experience, and it is recognizable by its dedicated space for AI-driven interactions designed to augment or replace manual effort.

name: Mini Player
description: The Mini Player design pattern is a compact interface element usually located at the bottom of the screen or in a corner. It takes up very little space and looks like a small bar or rectangle with a minimalist design. The mini player typically shows a small icon or thumbnail of the current media—such as an album cover, video preview, or podcast logo. Next to it, there are basic playback controls like play and pause buttons, sometimes with next or previous track buttons. It often includes a small progress indicator, like a bar or slider, showing how much of the media has played. You’ll also see the title or a brief description of the current track or video. There is usually a button or icon to expand the mini player into a full-sized player with more controls. Visually, the mini player is easy to identify by its small size, clear placement at the bottom or corner of the screen, and the presence of essential playback controls grouped together in a compact block.

name: Playlist
description: The Playlist pattern presents a curated or user-generated list of audio or video items arranged in sequence. Each item typically includes a title, thumbnail or cover image, duration, and play controls. The playlist interface may support reordering (often via drag & drop), adding/removing items, saving, and continuous playback. Often includes a “Now Playing” indicator and options like shuffle, repeat, or auto-play. Common in music apps, video platforms, learning modules, and media libraries.

name: Social Post
description: The Social Post design pattern is an interface element designed to allow users to share content, such as text, images, videos, or links, with others in a social or collaborative context. It is typically presented as a card or block that includes the user’s profile picture, name, and timestamp to indicate when the post was created. The main body of the post contains the shared content, which can range from simple text to multimedia elements or embedded links, often formatted for easy viewing. Social Posts also include interactive features like buttons for liking, commenting, sharing, or saving, enabling engagement and further interaction. Additional elements might include hashtags, mentions, or tags to categorize the content and make it discoverable. Posts can also display metrics such as the number of likes, comments, or shares, providing a sense of popularity or engagement. This pattern is common on social media platforms, forums, and collaborative tools, and it is recognizable by its structured layout designed to present user-generated content and encourage interaction.

name: Members
description: The Members pattern displays a list or grid of users associated with a team, group, project, or organization. Each member entry typically includes a name, avatar, role or permission level, and sometimes activity status or contact options. May include actions like add/remove member, change role, or message. Often appears in team settings, collaboration tools, or admin dashboards. Can support filters (e.g., by role) and sorting (e.g., alphabetically or by join date).

name: Bento Grid
description:
A Bento Grid is a type of layout used in design where items are arranged in small, flexible rectangles or squares. The unique thing about a Bento Grid is that the items don’t all have to be the same size. Some can be small, while others are big, but they all fit together like puzzle pieces. 

A Bento Grid is a layout system that divides content into distinct, modular sections, similar to how a bento box divides food into compartments.

Each section can vary in size and shape but is arranged in a structured tiles-like manner.

name: User Menu
description:
A User Menu is a design pattern used to give users quick access to account-related actions and settings. It’s typically located in the top-right corner of an interface and is often represented by an avatar, a profile icon, or the user’s name. When clicked or hovered over, it expands to reveal a dropdown or panel with options like viewing or editing the profile, account settings, logout, notifications, or switching accounts.

This pattern keeps the interface clean by consolidating account-related actions in one place while ensuring they’re easily accessible. Unlike global navigation menus or feature-specific controls, the User Menu focuses solely on personalized or user-specific options. It’s a common pattern in applications with authentication, as it helps maintain a clear separation between general app navigation and user account management.
